articles.title: Alcaraz se duele de la pierna izquierda y para el partido: "He notado algo en el isquiotibial"
articles.standfirst: El tenista domina por un set y 2-1 en el segundo set de su partido con Medvedev
articles.summary: El tenista domina por un set y 2-1 en el segundo set de su partido con Medvedev
articles.body: Han saltado todas las alarmas este miércoles en Turín cuando Carlos Alcaraz ha parado su partido ante Daniil Medvedev para ser tratado a la altura del muslo de la pierna izquierda. Ha vuelto a jugar con un aparatoso vendaje dominando el marcador, por un set de ventaja y 2-1 en la continuación. El tenista murciano entrena con protección en su rodilla derecha desde el primer día en Turín y se ayuda de un estabilizador rotuliano. Alcaraz ha llegado a la cita de maestros sin descanso después de encadenar títulos en Viena y en París. Cabe recordar que la superficie dura es la más agresiva para el cuerpo y Carlitos ha disputado en ella 11 partidos desde el pasado 27 de octubre. Alcaraz, después de su participación en la cita de maestros, es uno de los cinco convocados de España a la fase final de la Copa Davis (24 al 29). La selección nacional debuta el próximo jueves 26 contra Austria. David Ferrer ya se vio obligado a sustituir el lunes al lesionado Alejandro Davidovich por Dani Mérida. Carlitos ya se perdió las finales de la máxima competición por países en 2025 tras su participación en las ATP Finals donde alcanzó la final con Jannik Sinner. En ese caso fue por un edema en el isquiotibial. "He tenido problemas durante el partido, he notado algo en el isquio y he intentado no forzar al límite y jugar lo más relajado posible. He intentado estar tranquilo, muy concentrado en mis tiros y ser lo más agresivo posible desde el resto. He intentado estar concentrado al saque", confesaba a la conclusión. "Vamos a verlo con mi equipo". "Estaba jugando un grandísimo tenis y me vino el problema en el isquio. He notado algo. Menos mal que iba break arriba, que me ha ayudado a aceptar la situación, estar calmado y no hacer el loco. No estoy muy preocupado, los dos próximos días van a ser muy importantes", se sinceraba Alcaraz. Nada más terminar su comparecencia ante los medios de comunicación, el campeón de siete grandes se puso en manos de su fisioterapeuta, Juanjo Moreno. Será el quien quien evalúe los problemas físicos de su pupilo y dicte los pasos a seguir, entre otras cosas si se decide por descansar en la jornada de mañana.

articles.title: Alcaraz gana con susto a Medvedev y llama a la puerta de las semifinales
articles.standfirst: El murciano se anota la segunda victoria y es el líder del grupo Ivan Lendl en las ATP Finals
articles.summary: El murciano se anota la segunda victoria y es el líder del grupo Ivan Lendl en las ATP Finals
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha sumado este miércoles su segunda victoria en la fase de grupos de las ATP Finals de Turín y tiene pie y medio en las semifinales del sábado. El murciano se queda como líder del grupo Ivan Lendl tras superar a Daniil Medvedev, por 6-2 y 6-4, en 72 minutos. El mayor contrincante es ahora mismo su cuerpo. Y es que tuvo que ser vendado a la altura del muslo de su pierna izquierda tras el tercer juego del segundo set, cuando ya disfrutaba de un break de ventaja. "Es uno de los tenistas que mejor se mueve, junto a Djokovic, que hayamos visto nunca", reflexionaba en la previa Medvedev. El ruso se anotó el primer juego del partido en blanco porque su rival ganó el sorteo y eligió restar. Los largos intercambios despertaban la admiración de los 15.000 espectadores asistentes a la central del Inalpi Arena. El moscovita se quejaba porque le molestaban los llantos de un niño. La resistencia del pupilo del kazajo Andrey Golubev empezó a flaquear cuando entregó su servicio en el quinto juego. Fue con un revés a la red. Carlitos se sentaba en la silla de cambios y sonreía a su banquillo. Medvedev ya es la segunda mayor víctima de Carlitos en el circuito. Van ocho triunfos en 11 partidos, los mismos que tiene ante Tommy Paul. Sólo con Jannik Sinner venció más veces (10). Daniil, campeón en la edición de 2020, se presentó a la cita como líder en partidos ganados este curso en dura, con un total de 42. El pupilo de Samuel López ya le pisa los talones porque acumula 39. El número tres mundial juega a toda velocidad por entendimiento del tenis y porque quiere estar sobre el cemento el mejor tiempo posible. Cuatro juegos se le escaparon en el debut con Frances Tiafoe y esta vez fueron seis. Alcaraz, con el estabilizador rotuliano en su rodilla derecha, va lanzado hacia su primera corona de maestro. Encadena 12 triunfos en dura bajo techo y se mantiene invicto en ese hábitat en la presente campaña. Las finales de la Copa Davis se disputarán la semana que viene en las mismas condiciones. GreenSet, la marca española de pistas de tenis, tendrá listas las cuatro superficies de juego —la central y tres de entrenamiento— este mismo viernes. Al campeón de siete grandes le da igual la jerarquía de sus adversarios porque es mejor que cualquiera de ellos. De los seis duelos directos disputados con el top5 en 2026, sólo cedió la final de Montecarlo con Jannik Sinner. Es una lástima que no esté Jannik Sinner en liza porque la actual versión del fenómeno de El Palmar mejora incluso cualquier actuación realizada por el doble maestro de Turín ante su público. A falta de Jannik, Italia vibra con Carlitos.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev notified of lawsuit by former partner in abuse case during middle of ATP Finals
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev has been notfied about a lawsuit filed by his ex-partner during ATP Finals; world No 1 advanced to the semi-finals of the season-ending tournament on Tuesday night
articles.body:
The latest legal case brought by the mother of Zverev's former partner alleges the tennis player violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports news outlet L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told The Associated Press that Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honour had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to £208,484 €250,000 euros every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement . Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organisations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin.

Zverev has not commented on the lawsuit.

He previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020 and followed up in 2021 with a detailed account in a Slate.com article that was taken down because of a preliminary injunction issued by a German court. Slate said it stood by the article.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims. It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev Officially Notified of Lawsuit by Ex-Partner in Abuse Case
articles.summary: TURIN, Italy (AP) — Top-ranked tennis player Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.
articles.body:
TURIN, Italy (AP) — Top-ranked tennis player Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals on Wednesday.

The latest legal case brought by the mother of the former couple's daughter alleges that Zverev violated the terms of an out-of-court settlement between the pair after the woman accused him of assaulting her.

The lawsuit brought by Brenda Patea in Germany takes issue with Zverev reportedly saying in an interview with French sports daily L'Equipe earlier this year that "it has been proven that the accusations were false" and "my innocence has been proven."

Zverev's Berlin-based lawyers, Christian Schertz and Anna Sophie Heuchemer, confirmed in a statement shared with The Associated Press that they were formally served with Patea's lawsuit on Wednesday.

"Our client will defend himself against the lawsuit," Zverev's lawyers said. "If the statement attributed to him was indeed made in the form alleged, we consider it to be a permissible expression of opinion" protected by the German constitution.

They said there had been no breach of any contractual obligations.

Patea's lawyer, Michael Scheele, told The AP that Zverev's claim over his innocence "triggered a veritable storm of criticism against our client."

He said the backlash was damaging to her business as an influencer and that she also felt her honor had been violated.

"Quite apart from the fact that Zverev's claim is false, he was not permitted to make any public statements whatsoever, in any form," he said. "Both Brenda Patea and Alexander Zverev had agreed to this in a settlement."

Patea is seeking that Zverev be ordered not to repeat such comments and that he be fined up to 250,000 euros ($275,000) every time if he does.

Zverev faced a charge of causing bodily harm to Patea during an argument in Berlin in May 2020. He always denied any wrongdoing.

The case ended in a district court in Berlin in 2024 after the settlement. Zverev agreed to pay fines to the state and charitable organizations.

Zverev this month ascended to the No. 1 ranking for the first time. He also won his first two Grand Slam titles this year and is competing this week at the ATP Finals in Turin. His next match is on Thursday.

Zverev has not commented on the lawsuit.

It's not the first time that legal affairs have clashed with Zverev's tennis schedule. The settlement with Patea was decided while Zverev was playing the 2024 French Open. He did not appear in court then.

He previously denied abuse allegations from another former girlfriend, Olga Sharypova, who first made the accusations in 2020 and followed up in 2021 with a detailed account in a Slate.com article that was taken down because of a preliminary injunction issued by a German court. Slate said it stood by the article.

The allegations prompted the men's professional tennis tour, the ATP, to investigate her claims . It ended 15 months later, in January 2023, with the ATP saying there was "insufficient evidence" to substantiate the claims.

Associated Press Writer Geir Moulson in Berlin contributed to this report.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Alcaraz - Cobolli: horario y dónde ver en TV el tercer partido de las ATP Finals 2026
articles.standfirst: El murciano se impuso en el único precedente entre ambos en la primera ronda de Roland Garros 2023
articles.summary: El murciano se impuso en el único precedente entre ambos en la primera ronda de Roland Garros 2023
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz ha sumado su segunda victoria en el grupo Ivan Lendl de las ATP Finals de Turín 2026 tras acabar con la resistencia de Daniil Medvedev en dos rápidos sets. El murciano, que notó algo a la altura del isquiotibial de su pierna izquierda, ha iniciado una contrarreloj para estar en las mejores en lo que le resta de torneo. El cetro de maestro es uno de los dos grandes títulos que faltan a su palmarés, junto a la Copa Davis, que viene inmediatamente después en el calendario. Alcaraz afrontará este viernes su último partido del 'round robin' contra Flavio Cobolli, el número seis del ranking ATP a sus 24 años y el único italiano en liza en la competición individual. El español se impuso en el único precedente entre ambos hace tres años en la primera ronda de Roland Garros. La amistad entre Carlitos y Flavio llega al punto que el transalpino tiene una fotografía de los dos en el salvapantallas del móvil. El tercer partido de Carlos Alcaraz y Flavio Cobolli en las ATP Finals de Turín se celebrará en la central del Inalpi Arena este viernes 20, en un horario todavía por confirmar. El tercer partido de Carlos Alcaraz y Flavio Cobolli en las ATP Finals se podrá seguir a través de Movistar +, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición que reúne a los ocho mejores de la temporada. articles.title: ATP Finals: Carlos Alcaraz defies injury concerns to continue flawless run with win vs Daniil Medvedev
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz secured his spot in the knockout stages of the ATP Finals with a win over Daniil Medvedev; the Spaniard called for his physio after appearing to pull up with a hamstring problem; watch the ATP Finals live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
Seven-time Grand Slam champion Alcaraz extended his winning streak to 11 matches as he seeks a third consecutive indoor title after trophies in Vienna and Paris.

The Spaniard also secured a berth in the semi-finals of the eight-player event for back-to-back years after Frances Tiafoe beat home player Flavio Cobolli 7-6(8-6) 6-0 later on Wednesday evening.

Alcaraz's win was his fifth in six matches against top-five players this year. His lone loss came against Jannik Sinner in the Monte Carlo Masters final.

World No 1 Medvedev moves to a record of 1-1 for the tournament after he beat Cobolli on Monday.

Alcaraz 'feeling OK' despite medical timeout

After breaking Medvedev twice in the first set, Alcaraz was forced to call for treatment in the second set.

"I was playing great and suddenly I felt a little problem in my hamstring," Alcaraz said.

"But just a little bit. I mean, I could play really good tennis since that moment until the end of the match.

"I was trying to stay relaxed, to move not too aggressively.

"Right now I'm just feeling OK. We will see with my team, with my physio, but I think the rest of the day and tomorrow is really going to be important."

Alcaraz missed this year's French Open and Wimbledon after he was ruled out for four and a half months due to a right wrist injury.

Henman: Injury proves no distraction for Alcaraz

"I don't expect, even at this stage, he [Alcaraz] knows how serious this [injury] is.

"Whether he has been compensating, trying to protect his knee and now it's gone to his hamstring, his quad on the other leg.

"What could have been a distraction, just didn't really materialise, because his tennis is faultless.

"Where do you attack? He's so fast from the back of the court and is so good off both wings. He changes direction. You hit a great shot; he hits a slice back. He can stay in the rally and defend. His serving has been so consistent.

"We've seen him play like this on other surfaces; outdoors hard, on clay, on grass.

"But this level indoors is even new for him."

After suffering a 6-2 6-2 defeat at the hands of Alcaraz in his first match of the tournament, Tiafoe rebounded by fending off two set points in a first-set tiebreak to seal victory over Cobolli.

Having shaken up his diet and training regimen, Tiafoe has had the most consistent year of his career and reached the US Open semi-finals for a third time.

It was Tiafoe's first-ever victory at the ATP Finals, with the American making his debut at the event this year.

He will now go up against Medvedev on Friday for a spot in the semi-finals.

"I'm going to have to take it from him," Tiafoe said.

"I'm going to have to take it from him. He's going to make me earn it. He's going to make me execute it at the highest level.

"If I do that, I like my chances. If I don't, he'll get it done. It's that simple."

articles.title: Tennis star Sloane Stephens' Los Angeles home targeted by burglars
articles.summary: Three suspects are in custody. Stephens was not at home at the time.
articles.body:
Three men have been arrested in connection with a pair of burglary attempts in Los Angeles on Tuesday night, one of which was the home of tennis star Sloane Stephens .

Stephens, the 2017 U.S. Open champion, was not home at the time. According to her Instagram, she was in Cleveland on Monday night attending the Cavaliers game against the Chicago Bulls.

Police responded around 9 p.m. PT on Tuesday after a silent alarm was set off. When officers arrived, they found the front door had been destroyed.

According to the Los Angeles Police Department, two masked suspects shattered a glass door with a crowbar and entered inside. They were not scared off by barking dogs, but they did wake people inside who were housesitting for Stephens. After being confronted, the suspects left without taking anything.

The two men were later arrested following a car chase. Another person was also taken into custody, according to ABC7 , as they are accused of also burglarizing a Hollywood Hills home on Tuesday night.

Stephens, 33, has not played in a tennis tournament since September's Guadalajara Open in Mexico.

articles.title: La victoria de Tiafoe ante Cobolli clasifica a Alcaraz para semifinales como primero de grupo
articles.standfirst: El estadounidense se impuso al italiano en dos sets y se la jugará con Medvedev
articles.summary: El estadounidense se impuso al italiano en dos sets y se la jugará con Medvedev
articles.body: Frances Tiafoe, víctima de Carlos Alcaraz el lunes en la primera jornada del grupo Ivan Lendll, mantiene intactas sus opciones de clasificación tras derrotar este miércoles a Flavio Cobolli, por 7-6(6) y 6-0. El italiano queda eliminado y Tiaofe se la jugará el viernes con Daniil Medvedev. Cabe recordar que Flavio será el último rival de Carlos Alcaraz. Al jugador local le queda el consuelo de luchar por 200 puntos y 405.000 dólares. El triunfo del estadounidense clasifica a Alcaraz para semifinales y lo hace como líder. De esta forma se enfrentará en la penúltima ronda del sábado al segundo del grupo John McEnroe, a partir de las 14:30 horas. Carlitos podría evitar de esta manera a Alexander Zverev hasta una hipotética final. El alemán, campeón en las ediciones de 2018 y 2021, ha ganado sus dos primeros partidos sin perder un set y este jueves se mide a Arthur Fils.

articles.title: Alexander Zverev’s match with Ben Shelton at the ATP Finals angers tennis fans, ‘I feel so bad’
articles.summary: Alexander Zverev is the first player into the semifinals of the ATP Finals after a straight-sets win over Ben Shelton in Turin. But the encounter...
articles.body:
Alexander Zverev is the first player into the semifinals of the ATP Finals after a straight-sets win over Ben Shelton in Turin.

But the encounter between the two ATP superstars wasn't free of controversy, with many tennis fans angered by a statistic that emerged from the match between Zverev and Shelton .

It was confirmed that the ball was in play during the encounter between Zverev and Shelton for 10 minutes (active time), and one hour and 23 minutes in non-active time. Additionally, half the points in the ATP Finals tie ended in just one shot.

Tennis fans angry with Alexander Zverev match vs Ben Shelton

Sharing their dismay at the truly extraordinary figures, one tennis follower commented on X: "I feel so bad for the fans in the stadium."

A second fan agreed, saying: "Anyone who claims to love watching indoor tennis is lying to themselves and others," with a third noting: "Oh my ticket charge would be disputed!"

Others concurred with verdicts like: "Paying premium prices for poor quality matches. I'd be fuming," "And people wonder why they keep slowing courts down," and "How do people find this entertaining?"

The anger certainly didn't end there, with others making comments such as: "I'd rather watch clay tennis with no ELC with disputed points for 5 hours," and "Absolutely disgusting."

Summarising the thoughts of many, another fan said: "The best thing the ATP ever did was slow down the courts in the 00s and 10s so we'd get more rallies. The fact that they are actively choosing to make the sport worse to watch by speeding them up again makes zero sense."

Another said: "A match between these two wouldn't be entertaining on any surface of any speed. But it's still baffling to me that the Finals are played on what is basically an ice court. What is even the point?"

The bemusement is certainly understandable, and it looks set to continue as the tournament progresses. And intriguingly, the venue for the ATP Finals won't be changing anytime soon, with Turin set to host the year-end event until 2027. The indoor hard courts of the Inalpi Arena currently welcome the eight best ATP players in the world.

But perhaps action will be taken given the fan complaints, which followed a scintillating service display from Zverev in particular. The German, who triumphed 6-2, 7-6(7-4), won 25 points in a row behind his serve during the clash. He also fired down 14 aces, although his American opponent managed one more.

articles.title: Rennae Stubbs responds when asked if Serena Williams will return to tennis in 2027
articles.summary: Serena Williams made a triumphant return to tennis earlier this year. After months of speculation, the 23-time major singles champion returned to the court a...
articles.body:
Serena Williams made a triumphant return to tennis earlier this year.

After months of speculation, the 23-time major singles champion returned to the court at the Queen's Club Championships, playing alongside Victoria Mboko in the doubles event.

It was a successful return to competitive play for the American – she and Mboko defeated third seeds Erin Routliffe and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 7-6, 6-2. The duo were forced to withdraw from their next match following Mboko's season-ending injury.

Serena made her return to singles play a short while later, losing to Australian youngster Maya Joint in the Wimbledon first round.

The 45-year-old has not played a singles match since making an appearance at the All England Club.

Rennae Stubbs discusses whether Serena Williams will play singles matches in 2027

"I have no inside information whatsoever. I am not lying to you. I have no idea," Stubbs, Serena's coach, said on the Rennae Stubbs Tennis Podcast. "I saw Serena in New York at an event recently other than that I have no idea.

"I have not been on the tennis court with her. She is down in Florida and I live in New York.

"I think it is all dependent on how her body is feeling, if she wants to give it another go she will," the Australian 10-time major doubles champion added.

"But until she says yes I have no idea. That is the truth!"

Serena Williams' results since returning to the WTA Tour

Queen's Club Championships: Serena Williams and Victoria Mboko defeated third seeds Erin Routliffe and Nicole Melichar-Martinez 7-6, 6-2 in the first round. The duo were then forced to withdraw from the event after Mboko suffered a season-ending injury during a singles match.

Berlin Open first round: Giuliana Olmos and Erin Routliffe defeated Serena Williams and Karolina Muchova, 6-4, 6-4.

Wimbledon first round: Maya Joint defeated Serena Williams 6-3, 6-7, 6-3

Cincinnati Open first round: Marta Kostyuk and Peyton Stearns defeated Serena Williams and Venus Williams 6-2, 1-6, 10-8.

US Open first round: Hao-Ching Chan and Maya Joint defeated Serena Williams and Venus Williams 6-3, 6-7, 7-6.

Where could Serena Williams begin her 2027 WTA campaign?

If Serena decides to compete in singles, she could begin her 2027 campaign on January 4.

The American superstar, should she receive a wildcard, could play in either the ASB Classic or the Brisbane International. The events – last won by Xinyu Wang and Aryna Sabalenka, respectively – will both take place across the early part of January [ASB Classic from January 4 to 10, Brisbane International from January 3 to 10].

Serena could also make her return at either the Adelaide International or the Hobart International. Both events will run from January 11 to 16.

The Australian Open will take place following those events – from January 17 to 31.

articles.title: Retired at 25, inducted at 30! Ash Barty admits 'imposter syndrome' ahead of Hall of Fame honour
articles.summary: Ash Barty's tennis career ended at just 25, barely two months after winning the 2022 Australian Open.
articles.body: Ash Barty's tennis career ended at just 25, barely two months after winning the 2022 Australian Open. Five years later, the three-time Grand Slam champion is set to join the sport's immortals, but the former world No. 1 is still struggling to come to terms with the honour.Barty, now 30, has been elected to the International Tennis Hall of Fame (ITHF) and will be formally inducted at a ceremony in Newport, Rhode Island, next August. Yet, true to her understated nature, the Australian admitted she feels a little uncomfortable being placed alongside the absolute legends of the game."I feel very, very humbled and grateful. And to be honest, I've got a little bit of impostor syndrome where I feel I don't quite belong," Barty told Reuters. "The Hall of Fame is for the absolute legends of our game, and I'm not sure I'm quite there."The surprise announcement was made during a call with ITHF co-presidents Kim Clijsters and Patrick McEnroe. Barty was also touched by personal congratulatory messages from nearly 20 Hall of Famers, including Roger Federer and Martina Navratilova.Three Grand Slams, 114 weeks at No. 1Barty's achievements, however, leave little doubt about her place among tennis greats. She won three Grand Slam singles titles on three different surfaces, lifting the French Open in 2019, Wimbledon in 2021 and the Australian Open in 2022.Her Melbourne triumph ended Australia's 44-year wait for a homegrown women's singles champion. She also spent 114 consecutive weeks at the top of the world rankings.The Australian will be inducted alongside Japan's Shingo Kunieda, a four-time Paralympic gold medallist and 50-time major champion, who has been elected in the wheelchair tennis category.Barty said the recognition was as much for the people who supported her through her career as it was for her."I'm probably most excited to tell my team because it feels like it's as much for me as it is for them," she said.Her journey was far from straightforward, featuring struggles with depression, a nearly two-year break from tennis and a spell as a professional cricketer before she returned to the sport.'It was always never': No comeback plansBarty's retirement at 25, soon after the biggest triumph of her career, has repeatedly fuelled speculation about a possible comeback. But the Australian, now a mother of two, made it clear that she has no intention of returning to professional tennis.Asked whether her position had shifted from "never say never" to simply "never", she replied: "No, mate, it was always never."She also insisted she had no regrets about walking away from the sport at the peak of her powers."No, no, no, not one."Barty said she was fully immersed in family life and that her children were still unaware of her tennis achievements."My kids don't even know that I played tennis, and I'm sure that at the induction next year they'll wonder what's going on," she said. "I'm deep in the trenches with my two little ones at the moment, and I absolutely love it."Barty will become the second Indigenous Australian inducted into the Hall of Fame, after Evonne Goolagong Cawley, and hopes her recognition can inspire future generations."I think if you can provide the opportunity and the platform for them to learn and grow, then hopefully, maybe one day, there's another young boy or girl being inducted into the Hall of Fame," she said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Una resonancia magnética marca el futuro de Alcaraz en las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis
articles.standfirst: El tenista se examinará para ver el alcance de sus molestias en el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda. La prueba también revisará la rodilla izquierda
articles.summary: El tenista se examinará para ver el alcance de sus molestias en el isquiotibial de la pierna izquierda. La prueba también revisará la rodilla izquierda
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz se clasificó el miércoles para las semifinales de las ATP Finals como primero del grupo Ivan Lendl tras su segunda victoria en la fase de grupos tras apabullar a Daniil Medvedev, por 6-2 y 6-4. Sin embargo, el futuro del tenista en el torneo pasa ahora por una resonancia magnética, que se realizará este jueves a las 12.00 h, según ha podido saber MARCA. Las pruebas médicas, que serán este mediodía y examinarán su pierna izquierda (isquiotibiales y rodilla) marcarán sus opciones de título en la cita de maestros y de poder estar la semana que viene con España en la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29). La selección, que se concentra este sábado, debuta el próximo jueves 26 contra Austria. Muy pendiente de todo lo que pasa en Italia está David Ferrer, el seleccionador nacional de la Copa Davis, que tendría hasta el lunes 23 a las 11:00 de la mañana para encontrar un sustituto para el fenómeno de El Palmar. El lunes 16 ya se vio obligado a sustituir al lesionado Alejandro Davidovich por Dani Mérida. Carlitos ya se realizó una primera exploración el miércoles por la tarde, peno no se observaba nada porque había sido todo muy reciente. Al campeón de siete grandes le acompaña estos días en Turín Juanjo López, su médico de confianza y su fisioterapeuta Juanjo Moreno conoce cada centímetro de su cuerpo. "Los dos próximos días serán claves", advertía el número tres mundial tras su triunfo ante Medvedev. Lo que digan las pruebas y sus sensaciones permitirán saber los pasos a seguir. Alcaraz tiene el viernes un intrascendente partido en cuanto a la clasificación con Flavio Cobolli. Es cierto que sobre la mesa habrá 200 puntos más en el ranking que se mantienen durante toda la próxima temporada. Carlitos sintió algo en el isquio de su pierna izquierda en la pelota de rotura del primer juego del segundo set de su partido ante Medvedev. Aguantó dos juegos más y en el cambio pidió la presencia del fisioterapeuta para que le vendara en medio de un recital. La situación recuerda y mucho a la de hace apenas un año cuando el tenista tuvo dolor a la altura del isquiotibial, durante su segundo partido de la fase de grupos con Taylor Fritz. En ese ocasión siguió jugando, alcanzó la final vendado y un día más tarde se bajaría de las finales de la Copa Davis por un edema en el isquiotibial. Lo determinó la resonancia magnética que se hizo nada más llegar a Bolonia. "Son momentos que ya he pasado, que ya he vivido. Voy conociendo mi cuerpo cada vez más. Lo que necesito y lo que no y cómo debo afrontar estos momentos. La experiencia de haber pasado por este tipo de situaciones más de una vez es la que me hace saber cómo debo hacer las cosas tanto en el partido como fuera de la pista", contaba sobre el nuevo percance físico. Alcaraz luce un estabilizador rotuliano en su rodilla derecha desde su primer entrenamiento en Turín el pasado 11 de noviembre. Eso no le ha restado movilidad en los partidos. A pesar de ello, este jueves también se realizará pruebas médicas en la zona. Al segundo día de estancia en la capital de la región del Piamonte tuvo que irse de la sesión preparatoria antes de tiempo por un problema estomacal.

articles.title: Leandro Riedi: Tennis the saviour for player who tried to take own life
articles.summary: Swiss player Leandro Riedi tried to take his own life days before playing at Wimbledon in 2024. Now he wants to tell his story.
articles.body:
Warning: This article contains references to suicide

The clues were there. Leandro Riedi struggled to even force a smile after winning a match which moved him closer to the Wimbledon main draw.

These are the moments usually cherished and celebrated by a player ranked outside of the world's top 100.

The Swiss player's solemn reaction was jarring, but then nobody outside of his immediate circle knew what had happened a few days earlier.

Shortly before Wimbledon qualifying began in June 2024, Riedi had tried to take his own life.

Panic attacks had been plaguing the world number 137 for almost 18 months. Anxiety and self-doubt had been around for much longer.

The toll they were taking on his mental health meant he felt there was no other way out.

"I always had anxiety. I was always a shy person, especially when I was younger. I always had this mindset that I wasn't good enough," Riedi told BBC Sport.

"I always thought I needed to do something special. I have to be perfect. This was my mental battle all the time.

"February 2023 to November 2024 was a horrible period of time. I was always scared of having a panic attack. I had no control over it whatsoever."

Very few people knew the extent of Riedi's mental health issues until he revealed last week that he had attempted suicide.

The 24-year-old wants to make two things clear.

Firstly, he is not looking for sympathy. He has only decided to talk about his experience to "send a strong message" for others struggling with their mental health.

Secondly, he is now in a "very good" place, thanks to professional treatment he has received over the past two years.

"I hope nobody ever has to go through what I did - it's horrifying and scary," Riedi said.

"But I want to be an example it can turn out well."

The past - 'I don't know how I played at Wimbledon'

In his darkest moments Riedi found salvation in the sport which he started playing as a three-year-old growing up in Zurich.

"I felt really home at a tennis court - I was able to perform and I was able to play," he said.

"So tennis was my saviour in that time. It helped me to go out of my thoughts for one second and focus on doing what I love."

It goes some way to explaining why Riedi decided to still compete at Wimbledon so soon after attempting to end his life.

Looking back, he is unsure how he summoned the strength to play.

"My coach told me to go home. He was the only one who knew. But then what? Be sad at home?" Riedi said.

"I didn't want to go home. I wanted to stay and I wanted to play. It was a horrible, horrible week.

"After the first round I remember I just left and went to the hotel. Usually you're excited and happy about a win, but I couldn't speak."

In his hotel room Riedi continued to have troubled thoughts.

He credits his psychologist, who stayed awake with Riedi until 3am to make sure he was not alone, for saving his life.

Riedi went on to win his second qualifying match before losing in the third and final round. At first he felt the pressure was "lifted", but not competing created a void.

Riedi describes how he was "scared" to leave his hotel room for the next two weeks, only going out to collect food deliveries from the lobby.

Tennis continued to be the only force which Riedi thought provided purpose. He managed to leave London for a tournament in Sweden, banking on it "bringing happiness".

But, after winning a match in Gstaad, he started to realise that going on to court was merely a placebo effect.

The catalyst of change came a few weeks later when a knee injury - the first "big injury" of his career - required surgery following the US Open.

"It was devastating for me because I knew my one happiness - tennis - was gone," Riedi said.

"In tennis I always had to fight [my mental health] because I was still playing. I didn't want to show any weakness.

"Then I realised I didn't want to fight any more. I wanted to help it. I wanted to work with it."

The present - opening up to send 'strong message'

Focusing on tennis and receiving the support of his "closest people" helped Riedi through his most troubled times.

Reopening his psychological "wounds", and discussing his inner trauma with experts, has been the key to his recovery.

He no longer has suicidal thoughts. The panic attacks have stopped. He still has anxiety but possesses the coping mechanisms to prevent it being debilitating.

Riedi had been planning to open up publicly for several months. He still felt nervous when he hit publish on his social media post, but he has been heartened by an overwhelmingly warm response.

"I have got messages from all over the world. Someone texted me from India saying they saw the post and are going through something similar right now," Riedi said.

"They said 'Your message really helped me. It gave me some power to believe it's going to work.' That's exactly what I was aiming for.

"People think tennis pros have all they need. I wanted to showcase that it's OK not to be OK even though others think you have everything."

Riedi says his mental health struggles were caused by "private issues" in his life and were not a consequence of his career.

But, with players increasingly speaking out about mental burnout, he wants his words to drive further change.

The ATP already provides an in-house psychology and wellbeing service, which offers confidential support at tournaments and remotely.

If a mental health disorder prevents a player from competing for at least six months, they can apply for a protected ranking. It allows them to enter tournaments without penalty when they are ready to return.

Riedi says the governing bodies can "never do too much", but he thinks there is still an issue on the men's tour with reaching out for support.

"For me, mental health is like a muscle. If your knee is injured, you do surgery and take care of it," he said.

"If you're injured in your mind, it's like you can't speak about it. That's not good.

"I hope my message shows tennis players, or anyone, that speaking out isn't a weakness. It's actually the opposite. It's strong and brave."

The future - 'sky is the limit' after making peace

Since working on his mental health, Riedi has produced some of the best results of his career.

He came through qualifying to reach the last 16 of the 2025 US Open - his standout performance at a Grand Slam tournament - and climbed to a career-high world ranking of 116 this year.

The most poignant moment came in June 2025 when he returned to Wimbledon.

A year on from his suicide attempt, Riedi decided to stay at the same Chelsea hotel because he wanted "make peace" with what had happened.

"It was very emotional, but in a good way," he said.

"I was like, 'wow, when you really work on something, if you stay consistent about something, one year can do so much'."

This year Riedi's progress on the court has been hampered by a torn tendon in a wrist.

Being sidelined for six months led to some friends wondering why he does not stop playing professionally. He says his "love and passion" for tennis will not allow him.

Riedi says the "sky is still the limit" and plans to make his comeback at the start of 2027, using a protected injury ranking to enter Australian Open qualifying.

"I really had to go through big obstacles, but I'm very proud I did this at such a young age. I'm actually this guy who just likes life," he said.

"I love to do things. I want to be happy. I want to be excited for my future and not be scared."

If you have been affected by issues raised in this article, there is information and support available on BBC Action Line.

articles.title: Dani Mérida: "Si tengo que jugar, estaré listo seguro"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño ha reemplazado a Davidovich en la convocatoria de la selección nacional de la Copa Davis
articles.summary: El madrileño ha reemplazado a Davidovich en la convocatoria de la selección nacional de la Copa Davis
articles.body: La baja por lesión de espalda de Davidovich hizo que David Ferrer convocara de urgencia a Dani Mérida como quinto jugador para la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia. El madrileño habla con MARCA sobre cómo recibió la noticia y las ganas que tiene de afrontar la lucha por el título de la máxima competición por países. Pregunta. ¿Cómo recibió la noticia de su convocatoria? Respuesta. Me enteré hace un par de días cuando me llamó David para decirme que Alejandro no podría estar. Desde el primer momento, muy contento y muy feliz de ir a Bolonia y ayudar al equipo. P. ¿Se siente preparado? R. Sí, me siento preparado. Creo que he tenido una temporada buena y ya debuté en Chile por lo que me siento listo para ayudar al equipo en lo que me toque. Si es jugando pues jugando, y si es desde fuera, pues desde fuera. P. ¿La confianza del capitán lo ve como un premio a su año? R. Yo me lo tomo como un premio porque la Copa Davis es un torneo muy bonito para jugar, ya que defiendes a tu país. He tenido un año muy bueno y creo que me lo merecía. Le deseo una pronta recuperación a Davidovich. Yo estoy muy contento de estar. P. Tanto Carlos Alcaraz como Rafa Jódar, ambos presentes en Turín, andan físicamente tocados. ¿Se ve jugando las finales de Bolonia? R. He estado hablando con David y estaré preparado si tengo que jugar para dar el 100 por 100. Si tengo que saltar a pista, estaré listo seguro. P. Usted ya debutó en la Copa Davis en la anterior serie clasificatoria en Chile donde ganó a Alejandro Tabilo. ¿Se dio cuenta allí que es un jugador para este tipo de competiciones? R. Sí, a mí siempre me han gustado las competiciones por equipos. Sentir que juego para mi país te hace dar un extra. Estaré muy motivado si me toca jugar. P. ¿A usted no le da un extra de presión el tener a un país detrás? R. Claro que tienes nervios, como en todos los torneos y todas las primeras veces. Pero la motivación hace que saque lo mejor de mí en la pista. P. Durante el curso que ahora termina ha repetido en más de una ocasión la necesidad de viajar con un técnico. ¿Ya lo tiene para 2027? R. Sí voy a viajar con mi entrenador aquí en Alicante (Israel Sevilla), que no ha viajado este año. P. Primero dio el salto al ‘top 100’, después al ‘top 50’, ¿cuál es el objetivo para la próxima temporada? R. Lo he estado hablando esta mañana con mi equipo y queremos seguir creciendo en el ranking. Hay que empezar bien el año y el objetivo sería acabar cerca del top 10. Para eso hay que competir bien cada semana y mejorando varias cosas. Es un objetivo ambicioso, pero posible. P. ¿Es consciente de que con el equipo de España tiene una ocasión histórica de ganar la séptima Ensaladera de plata? R. Sí, sé que tenemos un equipo con grandes jugadores. Está Carlos, está Rafa, que viene de hacer un año increíble; Marcel y Pedro siempre dan un nivel muy alto en el dobles... Tenemos un equipo muy bueno, va a ser duro, pero contamos con grandes posibilidades de llevarnos el triunfo. Como se suele decir: hay que ir partido a partido. Ojalá terminemos la semana con el trofeo. P. Usted ha dado un salto de calidad en pista dura al aire libre. ¿Hay mucha diferencia respecto a jugar bajo techo? R. Cada semana cambia porque el indoor de Viena no es el de París. Son circunstancias diferentes. Y vamos a ver en Bolonia si es más rápido o más lento. Una cosa que he hecho bien este año es adaptarme a todas las superficies. Es lo que me llevó a competir. Hay que darlo todo con lo que nos encontremos. P. Muchos señalan a España como la gran favorita para relevar a Italia en el palmarés. ¿Usted acepta este cartel que les ponen? R. Sí que lo acepto. Pero esto es la Copa Davis y en todas las eliminatorias vamos a tener a rivales muy motivados. Si hacemos las cosas bien tenemos muchas posibilidades. P. ¿Cuándo se marcha para Bolonia? R. Este sábado nos vamos para allá y tenemos 4-5 días para adecuarnos a las circunstancias. Ojalá que estemos los cinco en plenas condiciones para competir porque va a ser un torneo muy bonito. P. ¿Ha tenido tiempo de hacer vacaciones después del Masters 1000 de París? R. He tenido unos 10 días de vacaciones, el año pasado fueron seis. Quería alargar un poco más las vacaciones, tres o cuatro días más, pero la llamada de David me ha motivado mucho y toca acortarlas. He empezado ya a entrenar y con muchas ganas de ir a Bolonia. P. ¿Cuál es su calendario en enero antes del Open de Australia? R. Mi idea era empezar las primeras semanas en Australia, en algún torneo 250. Ahora, con la convocatoria de la Copa Davis, que no tendré tantas semanas para entrenar, empezaré la semana antes del Open de Australia. Después, jugaré los torneos de tierra en Sudamérica.

articles.title: A qué hora es el Jódar - Shelton: horario y dónde ver hoy en TV el tercer partido de las ATP Finals 2026
articles.standfirst: Será el primer cara a cara entre el madrileño y el estadounidense en el circuito
articles.summary: Será el primer cara a cara entre el madrileño y el estadounidense en el circuito
articles.body: Rafa Jódar tiene este jueves una última oportunidad de clasificación para las semifinales de las ATP Finals de Turín que pasa por ganar en dos sets a Ben Shelton y esperar a que Alexander Zverev haga lo mismo con Arthur Fils. En ese caso habría un triple empate a una victorias y habría que acudir al porcentaje de juegos y sets ganados. Jódar, de 20 años y que ahora mismo cierra el 'top10', jamás se ha medido a Shelton, que ya no tiene en Turín la ayuda de Juan Carlos Ferrero. El número cuatro mundial viene de perder por séptima vez con Zverev, número 1 mundial. Rafa acumula 80 partidos jugados en el presente curso, de los que ganó 58. El tercer partido del grupo John McEnroe entre Rafa Jódar y Ben Shelton se disputará este jueves 19 de noviembre, en la central del Inalpi Arena, a partir de las 14:00 horas. Para la sesión nocturna, a las 20:30 horas, queda el duelo de Zverev y Fils. El tercer partido de Rafa Jódar y Ben Shelton en las ATP Finals se podrá seguir a través de Movistar Plus, plataforma que tiene los derechos de la competición que reúne a los ocho mejores de la temporada. En MARCA.com y Radio MARCA habrá una amplia cobertura con la mejor información.

articles.title: Ash Barty to be elected into International Tennis Hall of Fame next year
articles.summary: Three-time Grand Slam winner Ash Barty will be elected into the International Tennis Hall of Fame at a ceremony in August next year.
articles.body:
Australia's Ash Barty says she felt a sense of "impostor syndrome" after being elected to the International Tennis Hall of Fame.

The former world number one and three-time Grand Slam singles champion will be inducted at a ceremony in Rhode Island in August next year.

The 30-year-old joins an illustrious group of former players in the hall of fame, including Roger Federer, Billie Jean King and Margaret Court.

"I feel very, very humbled and grateful. And to be honest, I've got a little bit of impostor syndrome where I feel I don't quite belong," said Barty.

"The Hall of Fame is for the absolute legends of our game, and I'm not sure I'm quite there."

Barty announced her surprise retirement aged just 25 in 2022, less than two months after winning the Australian Open title.

That triumph made her the first home player to win the Australian Open men's or women's singles title in 44 years, having previously won the French Open in 2019 and Wimbledon in 2021.

Barty had also played cricket professionally in Australia's Women's Big Bash League when she took a break from tennis in 2014.

She will be the second Indigenous Australian in the hall of fame, following Evonne Goolagong Cawley, who won seven Grand Slam singles titles.

Now a mum of two, Barty said that she does not regret retiring at a young age and ruled out a comeback, saying she is happy focusing on her family.

"I'm probably most excited to tell my team because it feels like it's as much for me as it is for them," Barty added.

"My kids don't even know that I played tennis, and I'm sure that at the induction next year they'll wonder what's going on.

"I'm deep in the trenches with my two little ones at the moment, and I absolutely love it."

images.caption: Image caption, Ash Barty retired from professional tennis in 2022

articles.title: Alcaraz gana tiempo y saltará a jugar el último partido con Cobolli
articles.standfirst: El murciano está dispuesto a jugar vendado para llegar lo más lejos posible en el torneo
articles.summary: El murciano está dispuesto a jugar vendado para llegar lo más lejos posible en el torneo
articles.body: La voluntad de Carlos Alcaraz es la de seguir jugando en las ATP Finals por lo que hará lo que haga falta para que así sea. El murciano, después de pasar pruebas médicas este jueves en el Instituto de Medicina Deportiva de Turín, se ha convencido de saltar a la pista este viernes a disputar el último partido de la fase de grupos con Flavio Cobolli. La resonancia magnética mostró que puede seguir compitiendo, según ha podido saber MARCA. Lo que mostraban las imágenes no frenará al fenómeno de El Palmar. Las sensaciones con el paso de los días marcarán su futuro inmediato. Más que nunca hay que ir día a día. Junto a su equipo se quiere ir evaluando la situación jornada tras jornada. Al tenista le quedan un mínimo de dos partidos en la cita de maestros de Turín: el intrascendente para la clasificación ante Cobolli y las semifinales del sábado. Alcaraz aunque vendado, pudo seguir sin problemas durante el segundo set de su partido con Daniil Medvedev del miércoles. A esas sensaciones se agarra para seguir con el sueño de ser maestro ATP.

articles.title: Jódar planta cara a Shelton en su despedida de las ATP Finals
articles.standfirst: El madrileño tuvo dos pelotas para anotarse el primer set y ya mira a la Copa Davis de Bolonia
articles.summary: El madrileño tuvo dos pelotas para anotarse el primer set y ya mira a la Copa Davis de Bolonia
articles.body: Rafa Jódar, a sus 20 años, se marcha de su primera experiencia en las ATP Finals con la cabeza bien alta. El madrileño, en su primer año en el circuito, termina el curso como 'top10' mundial y plantando cara a los mejores. Rafa quedó este jueves eliminado de la cita de maestros al caer en su tercer partido de la fase de grupos ante Ben Shelton, por 7-6(8) y 7-5. Shelton será este sábado el rival de Carlos Alcaraz en las semifinales si Alexander Zverev suma un set en el duelo que cierra la jornada ante Arthur Fils. Jódar disfrutó de dos pelotas de primer set en el 'tie break', con 6-5 y 8-7. No las pudo aprovechar y por ahí que empezó a escapársele el tren de las semifinales. "Bien sacado", le decía Rafa senior a su hijo cuando igualaba a tres en la manga inicial. Servicio y tiro de derecha es lo que tiene para dar y para regalar Ben. Dos misiles a 230 kilómetros por hora evitaron la rotura del español en el quinto juego. Después disparó otro a mayor potencia, 235 km/h. Un pelotazo de Shelton en la espalda del joven de Leganés, que acabó tendido en el suelo, fue la antesala de la muerte súbita. Todos los puntos largos, los trabajados, caían del lado de Rafa. "Vamos", gritaba el madrileño, que se agarraba a sus escasas opciones de clasificación como a un clavo ardiendo. El set ganado por el estadounidense fue una pesada losa con 81 partidos a sus espaldas. Sin embargo, el carácter ganador de Jódar le llevó a remontar un 4-2 en el segundo set y estar a un juego de forzar un segundo 'tie break'. Todo terminó con una bomba de servicio. Queda un último esfuerzo para él con la fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29). Tiene un lugar seguro en los individuales del jueves contra Austria.

articles.title: ATP Finals: Ben Shelton beats Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of semi-finals
articles.summary: Ben Shelton battles past Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of a place in the ATP Finals last four.
articles.body:
Ben Shelton battled past Rafael Jodar to move within touching distance of a place in the ATP Finals last four.

US Open runner-up Shelton only lost his serve once but still had to fight for just over two hours to beat the fast-rising Spaniard 7-6 (10-8) 7-5.

American Shelton closed out the match with three aces in a row and then wrote "I'll be watching, Arthur" on the camera lens - a reference to the final game in the group.

Shelton will progress to the semi-finals if world number one Alexander Zverev beats France's Arthur Fils later on Thursday.

Fils would need to beat Zverev in straight sets if he is to qualify instead of Shelton.

"I think if he takes Sascha [Zverev] out in straights, I'll say too good and go on holidays," Shelton joked of his good friend Fils.

"I'm always rooting for him [Arthur] and I think he and Sascha will have a great match.

"I'd love to make the semi-finals for the first time. I'll definitely be watching."

Germany's Zverev, unbeaten so far at the season-ending event, is assured of top place in the John McEnroe Group, and will play either Daniil Medvedev or Frances Tiafoe in Saturday's semi-finals.

Shelton did not win a match on his ATP Finals debut last year, but arrived in Turin with a Masters 1000 title and a first Grand Slam final under his belt.

He beat Fils in three entertaining sets in his opening match before being swept aside by Zverev on Tuesday.

Shelton was under pressure against Jodar in the first set, saving two break points and missing a series of routine shots when his opponent was struggling.

However, after taking a tight tie-break, Shelton quickly broke to take control of the third set.

Jodar, competing in his first professional season on the ATP Tour, was strong defensively and wrestled the break back to level at 4-4.

However, he was visibly fatigued and unable to keep Shelton at bay in a series of lengthy rallies, with Shelton breaking for 6-5.

Shelton slipped at the back of court as he served for the match, but recovered quickly to close out victory. He finished with 14 aces to one double fault, having dropped only 11 points behind his first serve.

In the doubles, Britain's Henry Patten and Finnish partner Harri Heliovaara will need to beat French pair Theo Arribage and Albano Olivetti if they are to keep their title defence alive.

Wimbledon champions Patten and Heliovaara have won one and lost one of their three group matches.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar y el futuro al lado de su padre: "No veo ninguna razón para cambiar nada"
articles.standfirst: El madrileño reconoce que tiene el mes de diciembre para valorar las mejoras de cara al futuro
articles.summary: El madrileño reconoce que tiene el mes de diciembre para valorar las mejoras de cara al futuro
articles.body: rafa Jódar ha terminado oficialmente su primera temporada en el circuito ATP y lo ha hecho con buena nota, aunque a él no le gusta calificarse. Al madrileño, de 20 años, le queda ahora la ilusionante fase final de la Copa Davis de Bolonia (24 al 29) donde España debuta el próximo jueves 26 contra Austria. Equipo con su padre en 2027. "Las cosas han funcionado muy bien este año con mi padre en el equipo. No es fácil cuando él tiene que trabajar cada semana. No veo ninguna razón para cambiar nada, pero al mismo tiempo, queda un mes para pensar en las cosas que podemos mejorar para la temporada que viene. Hay muchas cosas que valorar y poner en perspectiva. Estoy muy agradecido a mi padre por todo lo que ha hecho por mí este año. No sé todavía lo que va a pasar en 2027". Balance de la temporada. "Estoy muy orgulloso de lo que he hecho esta temporada. No me he dejado ir en ningún partido. Cuando las cosas han ido mal en los partidos siempre he intentado buscar soluciones. Como hoy, por ejemplo, que iba break abajo en el segundo set. He creído en mi hasta el último momento aunque al final no salió". Nota del curso. "Prefiero no ponerme nota porque no me gusta. Cuando te pones nota siempre estás pensando en superar esa nota. Sé que he hecho las cosas bien y que he disfrutado mucho en los torneos en los que he estado. El objetivo, al principio de la temporada, era conocer todos los torneos. Poder competir con los mejores jugadores del mundo y ese objetivo lo he cumplido. Estar aquí en las ATP Finals significa mucho para mí. Tengo claro que puedo ser mejor jugador y que, en momentos importantes, puedo ser más competitivo". La Copa Davis, en el horizonte. "La afronto con mucha ilusión porque sé que es muy difícil ser convocado para jugar porque en España hay mucha competencia porque tenemos a grandes jugadores. Le tengo muchas ganas. El equipo está muy unido, lo pude ver en la eliminatoria de Chile. Veo que todos tenemos muchas ganas de conseguir la Copa Davis. Hay que dejarse todo en la pista".

articles.title: A España ya le espera la pista de la Copa Davis de Bolonia
articles.standfirst: La empresa española GreenSet ha hecho las cuatro pistas de la fase final de la máxima competición por países
articles.summary: La empresa española GreenSet ha hecho las cuatro pistas de la fase final de la máxima competición por países
articles.body: La selección nacional de la Copa Davis, que se concentra este sábado en la ciudad de Bolonia para preparar la fase final de la máxima competición por países (24 al 29), ya sabe que las pistas están terminadas y listas para los entrenamientos previos al debut el próximo jueves 26 contra Austria. El conjunto de David Ferrer empezará las sesiones de trabajo este domingo. La empresa española GreenSet, liderada por Javier Sánchez Vicario, ha elaborado las cuatro canchas presentes en la Feria de Bolonia: la central y tres de entrenamiento. GreenSet es líder mundial en superficies de tenis, como lo demuestra el hecho que también están presentes en las ATP Finales de Turín y antes en el Masters 1000 de París. De esta forma, los jugadores que hacen doblete en los dos torneos que cierran el curso no notarán mucho cambio entre superficies.

articles.title: It is clear who should win Great Britain’s best female player of 2026 as the nominees are announced
articles.summary: The nominees for the Lawn Tennis Associations’ Women’s Player of the Year award have been announced. Katie Boulter, Sonay Kartal, Harriet Dart, Emma Raducanu...
articles.body:
The nominees for the Lawn Tennis Associations' Women's Player of the Year award have been announced.

Katie Boulter , Sonay Kartal, Harriet Dart, Emma Raducanu and Francesca Jones have all been nominated for the award.

Two of the nominees – Katie Boulter and Harriet Dart – have won WTA Tour-level events this year. Emma Raducanu has reached the final at two events, while Sonay Kartal stunned the tennis community by qualifying for the Wuhan Open final last month.

Francesca Jones has also enjoyed a stellar year on the circuit, winning WTA 125 events in Palermo and Rome.

Who is the most deserving winner of this award?

Katie Boulter should win the LTA's Women's Player of the Year award

Katie Boulter has been the most consistent British player on the WTA Tour this year.

The British player won her fourth WTA event in March, beating Tamara Korpatsch 5-7, 6-2, 6-1 in the Ostrava Open final.

Boulter also achieved excellent results against some of the best players the WTA Tour has to offer, including defeating Leylah Fernandez and Elena Rybakina en route to the Queen's Club Championships semi-finals.

Of course, all other nominees have enjoyed high points throughout the 2026 campaign. For example, Emma Raducanu qualified for finals in Romania and London, and Harriet Dart won her first Tour title in Guangzhou, China .

However, none of the other nominees have come close to matching Katie Boulter's consistency across the 2026 season.

This argument is supported by Boulter's year-end ranking: she is the British number one and has halved her ranking when compared to the same stage of last season.

Katie Boulter's 2026 WTA Tour tournament results

Boulter, now ranked 50th on the Tour, sat in the 100th position at the end of last season.
